problems: The new negative TCF3 and ETS1 ChIP-seq results (E25/E26) concern assayed biosamples other than the inferred glioblastoma context; they do not establish absence of occupancy in glioblastoma or contradict the stated lack of matched-biosample ChIP-seq.
The QBiC-SELEX results support only predicted allele-dependent in-vitro binding. None of the cited evidence establishes in-cell occupancy by the nominated TF or resolves the acting family member.
The enhancer-feature annotation and TERT promoter-interval overlap do not establish regulatory activity at the variant; the variant does not overlap an ENCODE cCRE.
TERT remains a plausible nearby candidate, but the L2G result is for hypertension with PIP 0.00, and there is no significant GTEx eQTL or molecular-QTL evidence cited here.
General literature on TERT promoter alterations in glioblastoma does not link this allele to glioblastoma, melanoma, or bladder disease. The failed gene_disease lookup (E27) supplies no evidence.

checks.why: Checks whether ENCODE has a TCF3 peak containing this variant, which could strengthen or weaken the in-cell occupancy link.
Checks for ETS1 occupancy at the variant, helping distinguish the ref-favoring ETS hypothesis from the alt-favoring TCF3 hypothesis.
Examines the evidence types behind a TERT association with the case disease, which could change how plausible the proposed target-to-phenotype link is.

critique.next_experiment: In an appropriate glioblastoma model, create isogenic G and A alleles and measure allele-specific TF occupancy together with TERT expression; this would test whether the in-vitro binding predictions translate into occupancy and a target-gene effect.
